text: The four registry tables carry the field names the legacy story fixes, with a state, a valid-from and valid-to date, the author, the approver, the loaded and approved times, the workbook reference, the generated DRL, a SHA-256 checksum, the test result, the dry-run counts and the rollback pointer; the physical types, the nullability and the unique and index keys are taken from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary at implementation.
why: The load, the state moves, the checksum comparison and the one-call rollback cannot be built or tested without a state, two dates, an author, an approver, an artifact reference and a content hash, and no source gives their physical form.
read: TSD P7 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 11 and 13; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15
confirm: P7 solution architect and the owner of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON at the model contract review
impact: Column names, types and keys only; the six states, the checks, the promotion time, the checksum refusal and every criterion stay unchanged

text: The dry run reads the open case facts from rwb-case through one paged REST read, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases, filtered by status and paged, under the contract RWB-P3-E1073-CON with a 2 s one-hop timeout, and stores counts only.
why: The dry run needs the product group, queue, region, exposure band and deviation flag of every open case, the legacy read them in process, and no source names the operation.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 11 and 13; Ownership Map v1 P3 provided operations; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11
confirm: P3 and P7 contract owners at the rwb-case contract review
impact: One path, its filters and its paging only; the counts, the criteria and the no-case-fact rule stay unchanged

text: The promotion is announced as rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 on rwb.decision.events.v1, keyed by the package code, carrying the package code, the version label, the in-force time and the version SHA-256, through the outbox of DP-09; the identifier it takes among EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 is fixed in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog.
why: P7 owns three events and no source names one of them as the rule-package announcement, and the owning services cannot learn of a version in force without a named event.
read: TSD P7 T5.3; Ownership Map v1 P7 events; Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-14
confirm: P7 solution architect and the event catalogue owner at the next catalogue version
impact: One event name and one payload; the promotion, its time and every criterion stay unchanged

text: rules.testcases.min stands at 50 as the legacy story assumes it, is read as a parameter through the client library of DP-06, and is never written in code; the guard refuses a load whose Tests tab holds fewer scenarios.
why: The story requires at least that many scenarios on every load, the legacy marks the value assumed, and no parameter catalogue holds a confirmed value.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3, 8 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06
confirm: P3 parameter owner and RW-COE at the first package load
impact: A parameter value only; the guard, its refusal and the test data stay as written, and the value can change without a release

text: The six registry operations and their controller live in rwb-decision, in the modules rulepackage and rulepackageadmin, and the rights they check stay rows of the rwb-access role model; the move out of the legacy access module is recorded in the Change Register.
why: The legacy story places the operations in the access module of the monolith while the Ownership Map gives them to P7, and the target keeps one deployable service per module.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 12 and 13; Ownership Map v1 P7 and P4 rows; Template and Rules R3
confirm: P7 solution architect and the Ownership Map owner
impact: Code location and module names only; the paths, the rights and every criterion stay unchanged
